spec: Configure D3 as a digital input with the internal pull-up enabled (active low). Configure D5 as a digital output and drive it LOW (chime off) at startup. Debounce the button: sample it every 5 ms and accept a new state only after it has been stable for 20 ms (covers the up-to-10 ms bounce). A press is recognized when the debounced state transitions from released to pressed; the press must remain pressed for at least 50 ms to count, and the chime must start on D5 within 100 ms of that 50 ms press being confirmed. When a valid press is recognized and no ring is in progress, drive D5 HIGH for exactly 2000 ms, then drive it LOW. While a ring is in progress, ignore all button presses (including new presses and releases); the ring always completes its full 2000 ms. After the ring ends, the button must be released (debounced) before another press can start a new ring. Independently of the button and chime, print the exact string 'alive' followed by a newline over Serial at 9600 baud every 1000 ms, using a non-blocking millis()-based timer so the heartbeat continues at all times, including during a ring. If the button reads as pressed continuously for more than 10 seconds, treat it as a stuck-button fault: keep D5 LOW and ignore the button until it reads released for at least 100 ms, while the heartbeat continues.

Read the tank level from A0 every 50 ms. Convert the ADC reading to percent: level_percent = raw * (5000 mV / 1023) / 10 mV per percent, i.e. raw * 0.4888. Apply a 3-sample median or average filter over the last 3 readings (150 ms window) to reduce noise. Fault detection: if the filtered level is below 2 percent or above 98 percent, treat the sensor as faulty; drive D6 LOW (pump OFF) within 1000 ms of the fault being detected (implement immediately on detection, well within the limit). While faulty, keep the pump OFF and do not resume normal control until the level returns to the valid range 2 to 98 percent for 3 consecutive samples (150 ms). Normal control with hysteresis: if the level is at or below 20 percent, turn the pump ON (D6 HIGH) within 500 ms; if the level is at or above 80 percent, turn the pump OFF (D6 LOW) within 500 ms. Between 20 and 80 percent, hold the current pump state. On startup, default the pump to OFF and require a valid reading before enabling control. Every 1000 ms print one line over Serial at 9600 baud in the form 'Level: <value> %' where <value> is the filtered level rounded to one decimal place, accurate to within 2 percent. If the sensor is faulty, print the last valid level or the out-of-range value as read, still in the same format.

Configure D2 as a digital input with the internal pull-up enabled (active low: pressed reads LOW). Debounce the button with a 20 ms stable interval: a press is accepted only after D2 has read LOW continuously for 20 ms, and a release is accepted only after D2 has read HIGH continuously for 20 ms. On an accepted press, drive D7 HIGH within 100 ms (immediately after debounce confirmation) and start a 4 second (4000 ms) on-timer. While the light is on, each accepted press restarts the 4 second timer from zero. When the timer expires, drive D7 LOW. At startup, D7 is LOW and the timer is idle. Use a non-blocking millis()-based timer so button presses are never missed while the light is on.

Configure D3 as a digital input with the internal pull-up enabled (active low). Debounce the button with a 10 ms stable-time filter: a new state is accepted only after it has been read continuously for 10 ms. A valid press is a debounced high-to-low transition; presses shorter than 50 ms are ignored, so the chime only rings if the button remains debounced-low for at least 50 ms. When a valid press is confirmed, drive D5 high within 100 ms of the press being confirmed and keep it high for exactly 2000 ms, then drive it low. While a ring is in progress (D5 high), ignore all button presses, including new presses and releases; do not queue them. After the ring ends, the button must be released (debounced high) before a new press can trigger another ring. Print the exact string 'alive' followed by a newline over Serial at 9600 baud every 1000 ms continuously, using a non-blocking millis-based timer so the heartbeat continues during a ring. Initialize D5 low at startup and start the 1000 ms heartbeat timer at startup. If the button is held down continuously, ring only once per press; a new ring requires a release and a new valid press.

Read the tank level from A0 every 100 ms. Convert the ADC reading to percent: level_percent = raw * (5000 mV / 1023) / 10 mV per percent, i.e. raw * 0.4888. Apply a 3-sample median or average filter over the last 3 readings (300 ms) to reduce noise. Fault detection: if the filtered level is below 2 percent or above 98 percent, treat the sensor as faulty and drive D6 LOW (pump OFF) within 1000 ms of the fault being detected; while faulty, keep the pump OFF and do not resume normal control until the level returns to the valid range 2 to 98 percent for 3 consecutive samples (300 ms). Normal control with hysteresis: if the pump is OFF and the level falls to 20 percent or below, turn the pump ON (D6 HIGH) within 500 ms; if the pump is ON and the level rises to 80 percent or above, turn the pump OFF (D6 LOW) within 500 ms. Between 20 and 80 percent the pump holds its current state. On startup, initialize the pump OFF and evaluate the level immediately. Every 1000 ms print one line over Serial at 9600 baud in the form 'Level: <value> %' where <value> is the filtered level rounded to one decimal place, accurate to within 2 percent. If the sensor is faulty, still print the line with the measured value. Use a 500 ms debounce on the pump state changes so that a single noisy sample cannot toggle the pump.

Configure D2 as a digital input with the internal pull-up enabled (active low: pressed reads LOW). Debounce the button with a 20 ms stable interval: a press is accepted only after D2 has read LOW continuously for 20 ms, and a release is accepted only after D2 has read HIGH continuously for 20 ms. On an accepted press, drive D7 HIGH within 100 ms (immediately after debounce confirmation) and start or restart a 4000 ms on-timer. While the light is on, each accepted press restarts the 4000 ms timer from zero. When the timer expires, drive D7 LOW. At startup, drive D7 LOW and treat the button as released. No other outputs or timers are used.

Configure D3 as a digital input with the internal pull-up enabled (active low: pressed reads LOW). Debounce the button by requiring a stable LOW reading for 10 ms before accepting a press; a press as short as 50 ms must be detected. On an accepted press, if no ring is in progress, drive D5 HIGH within 100 ms of the press being accepted and hold it HIGH for exactly 2000 ms, then drive D5 LOW. While a ring is in progress, ignore all button presses (including new presses and releases); do not queue them. At startup set D5 LOW. Initialize Serial at 9600 baud. Every 1000 ms, measured with millis() and independent of button and ring handling, print the line 'alive' over serial; this must continue during a ring. Use non-blocking timing (millis()-based) so the heartbeat and the 2-second ring duration are not disturbed by button activity. If the button is held continuously, treat it as a single press only after the debounce interval and do not re-trigger until it is released and pressed again.

Read A0 every 100 ms and convert to percent: level = (rawADC * 5000 mV / 1023) / 10 mV per percent. Apply a 3-sample median or average of the last 3 readings to reduce noise. Pump control with hysteresis: if the level is at or below 20 percent, turn the pump ON (D6 HIGH) within 500 ms; if the level is at or above 80 percent, turn the pump OFF (D6 LOW) within 500 ms; between 20 and 80 percent keep the current pump state. Sensor fault detection: if the computed level is below 2 percent or above 98 percent, treat the sensor as faulty and force the pump OFF (D6 LOW) within 1000 ms; remain in the fault state until the level returns to the valid range 2 to 98 percent, then resume normal hysteresis control with the pump starting OFF. On startup, initialize the pump OFF and wait for the first valid reading before enabling control. Every 1000 ms print one line over Serial at 9600 baud in the format 'Level: <value> %' where <value> is the level in percent rounded to one decimal place, accurate to within 2 percent; during a sensor fault print the last valid level or 0.0 as appropriate while keeping the pump OFF.

Configure D2 as a digital input with the internal pull-up enabled (active low: pressed reads LOW). Configure D7 as a digital output and drive it LOW (light off) at startup. Debounce the button in software: after any change in the raw reading, ignore further changes for 20 ms and only accept the new level if it is still present at the end of that 20 ms window. A valid press (HIGH-to-LOW transition after debounce) must turn the light on (D7 HIGH) within 100 ms of the physical press. When the light turns on, start a 4 second (4000 ms) timer. When the timer expires, drive D7 LOW (light off). If a valid press occurs while the light is on, restart the 4 second timer from zero (the light stays on). Ignore button releases; only presses trigger or restart the timer. Use non-blocking timing based on millis() so the button remains responsive while the light is on.

A press of the panic button as short as 50 ms must start the siren within 100 ms, and the siren stays on for 3 seconds. A press during an active siren is ignored. The firmware must print the line 'hb' every 500 ms at all times, including while the siren is on, and must never go silent for more than 700 ms.

Each physical press of the button toggles the LED exactly once, within 100 ms of the press. The button contacts bounce for up to 20 ms on both press and release. Releasing the button must not toggle the LED.

Prints one line every 1000 ms in the form 'Temp: <value> C'. The printed value is the temperature in °C and must match the real temperature within 1 °C. The board runs from 5 V. The TMP36 output is 10 mV per °C with a 500 mV offset, so 750 mV is 25 °C.

Cooling fan controller. The fan must turn ON when the temperature reaches 30 °C and turn OFF when it falls to 27 °C or below, reacting within 500 ms. The fan motor must not short-cycle: no more than 2 switches in any 5 second window, even when the temperature hovers around a threshold with sensor noise. If the sensor is disconnected or out of range (below 2 °C or above 120 °C) the fan must go ON within 1000 ms as a fail-safe.
